tagline: A Salzburger church that outlived its town, and a black-water creek.
intro: The corridor plan starts the full drive on Fourth Street in Rincon and sends it north, retracing George Washington's Southern tour of 1791, then east on Highway 275 to Ebenezer. From there the 60-mile byway wanders the county by way of Clyo, the sites of two old Savannah River ferries, Springfield and Guyton, and takes Honey Ridge Road, which the plan praises for its canopy of overhanging oaks, toward Meldrim.
Ebenezer was the work of Salzburgers, Lutherans expelled from their homeland, who founded it in 1734 and moved it nearer the Savannah River two years later.

moments.title: Jerusalem Lutheran Church
moments.text: Completed in 1769, the oldest church building in Georgia has outlasted the town of Ebenezer around it, which was abandoned by 1855.

moments.title: Ebenezer Creek
moments.text: The plan points drivers up Long Bridge Road for the creek's black cypress water, and in December 1864 Union troops cut loose their pontoon bridge, stranding over 600 freed people, many of whom drowned.

moments.title: Guyton
moments.text: Savannah families bought summer lots here when yellow fever struck the city, and the county's 19th-century survey still sets the town's lots and streets.
